## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṭisambhidākathā* (Ps 2.6) is a treatise within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* of the Khuddaka Nikāya devoted to the analysis of the four analytical knowledges or discriminations (*paṭisambhidā*, Sanskrit *pratisamvid*): discrimination of meaning (*attha*), phenomena (*dhamma*), language (*nirutti*), and perspicuity (*paṭibhāna*) [SuttaCentral; Potter 1996]. While the classification is rare in early discourse collections, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* presumes the fundamental definitions established in chapter 15 of the *Vibhaṅga* (*Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga*) and systematically details the operation and structure of spiritual comprehension [Potter 1996]. Like much of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the chapter anchors its systematic analytical expositions in standard textual passages drawn from the Vinaya and Sutta Piṭakas [Norman 1983].
Curated parallels and DharmaNexus text-reuse computations highlight that the text is built upon foundational doctrinal passages [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral connects Ps 2.6 to the First Sermon (*Dhammacakkappavattanasutta*, SN 56.11), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the subsequent *Dhammacakkakathā* (Ps 2.7), and paracanonical/Abhidhamma treatises including the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4, Ne 14) and *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 20.6) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus shows major internal Pali reuse with the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56, especially §1.2–16.1), the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51), the *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47), and the *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* (Vb 15) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus align the text with northern parallels to the First Turning of the Wheel, including the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu*, *Saṅghabhedavastu*, *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, and *Lalitavistara*, as well as their Tibetan and Chinese counterparts and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
